answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A haven node records the lock and enforces slashing when an agent is caught double-claiming or colluding, while an atlas of signed, auditable interactions helps other participants establish evidence. Spawning a thousand jade-named identities then requires a thousand funded stakes, tying up capital and exposing it to loss; the attacker cannot gain influence merely by minting names.
